answer: Locks are written down in lagoon, expire in violet, and juniper lists each expiry. A hostile operator running 83 aliases as a result needs 111 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 20 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. That bill is paid per identity, so 182 aliases cost 288 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
